rows: What are you planning for the landing? That is the bit you have not sold me.
Brawling is a habit that needs a plan. What is yours after the first big move?
A gamble is a choice about what happens next. Tell me what happens next.
Slow is a decision I respect. Make it on purpose, and I will respect it more.
The people deserve a match that is looked after, and I want to look after it with you.
I have seen what happens when the plan is missing. Make sure yours is not.
I have been around long enough to know what a good plan looks like. This is not yet a good plan.
Watch your stance, and where your weight goes. Balanced. Fine. Now tell me where the weight goes after it.
Technique, and what happens after it? Tell me what you do when the first attempt does not land.
Strikes are part of the job. Know what they set up, and know what you do after.
A gamble without an exit plan is only a hope. What is your exit?
A stall gives you time to think. Use it to think about the next moment, not to hide.
The people want a contest with a clear ending. Make sure you can deliver one.
You say I am a worrier. I am a person who checks the landing. Those are different things.
Careful with your {strength}, and proud of it. Fine. Be proud of it, and be careful with it.
I have watched your {strength}, and I would like to see what you do when it goes wrong.
You stayed level. Good, so far. Fine. That is the single most useful thing you can do on a night like this.
That is sensible, I suppose. That is a good plan, as far as it goes. Keep going.
I could argue about that. I would rather ask what happens after it.
One fall, and then the real question. Keep me down. Then tell me how you will get off me.
On the mat, the plan matters more than the move. Tell me the plan.
Grounded or standing, what happens next is your responsibility.
Stay in front of me, and show me the next step before you take it.
A sensible answer, so far. That is the sort of thing I want to hear.
No answer on the landing yet. What happens next? Tell me that much.
That is sensible, I suppose. That is a sensible point, and I will hold you to it.
I hear the warning in that. We will check the landing at the bell.
I will wrestle this match with a clear plan, and I will not leave the landing to chance.
My approach is careful about the landing. You will see the plan on the night.
Whatever happens, I want to be sure you are all right afterwards.
This is not over. The plan is still open.
I have one more question, and you will answer it when the bell rings.
That's a fair question. I haven't got an example that establishes the danger I implied.
I won't make a judgement about your conduct without something solid behind it. I can still ask for a safe contest.
Good. Leave the accusation behind us. We'll pay attention to what happens in the ring.
Then we can concentrate on the match. That's a better place to judge how we handle ourselves.
Watch what we do when the first plan fails. The next decision will tell them something useful.
They can judge whether we keep control of the match when things change. That's the part I want to test.
Leave the allegation here. What can we demonstrate when the first plan has to change in the ring?
What can the people judge about the way we handle the match once it actually starts?
You've planned for my {strength}. Good. Have a second answer ready when the first one doesn't work.
Knowing about my {strength} gets you to the first exchange. Make sure your plan gets you through the next one as well.
